reviews.text: The Contractor is one more generic action flick with a story borrowed directly from the formulaic Hollywood closet, without any surprises or even high entertainment levels.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: ...the picture’s slow-but-steady descent into irrelevance is triggered by a generic and rather bland midsection...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The further it goes down the genre route the more it loses its relevance. And as an action movie, Saleh never fully gets the film off the ground. So it isn’t as pertinent as it tries to be or as kinetic as it wants to be.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: With mostly stale action and a bungled third act missing usual political intrigue, The Contractor feels like a knockoff of better, mid-2000s fare.
reviews.author: Michael Frank

reviews.text: Good cast in this thrilling and well-made shoot-em-up action drama starring Chris Pine where dialogue reveals the characters reservoirs of pain and existential fears.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: A standard operating procedure is employed by The Contractor.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The easy mesh of the actors sells us the relationship: Foster the tinder-dry joker to Pine’s quiet man.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: The Contractor posits that our capitalistic system absolutely prioritizes the almighty dollar above our humanity, and keeps us rooting for our hero to prove his innate value against a stacked deck.
reviews.author: Ed Travis

reviews.text: Solid espionage thriller, which moves confidently and convincingly through the same shadowy recesses of covert spy-guy activity.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text:
What would have been a direct to DVD, is more so made direct to stream. 
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: All the work the actors put into elevating the script, though, ends up doing nothing. "The Contractor" is as bland as its title, with not even one exciting action sequence to its credit.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: There’s a tense, tightly constructed thriller here — and Chris Pine makes a decent play as a neo-Bourne.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: [A] diverting if predictable espionage flick...
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Pine is good at humanising this trope. Guilt and regret course through his character and he never just shakes off his physical ailments, which helps give the action sequences a frisson of danger.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The Contractor is as generic and dull as its title, with an over-used action-movie plot of a bitter military veteran who goes rogue. Throw in some 'daddy issues,' sloppy editing, and a drab Chris Pine -- and that sums up this soulless film.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: By following predictable patterns, The Contractor does its job acceptably by providing brief but forgettable distraction.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: While the plot doesn't stand up to scrutiny, some decent action sequences at least keep things interesting.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Once the story begins to come together, it doesn't really hold together... But you forgive it just because Chris Pine is just so friendly to spend time with.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: This movie doesn't know if it's trying to be that direct action movie or if it's trying to deconstruct the plight of the American soldier.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Chris Pine, Ben Foster and Kiefer Sutherland - great star power for what is only an average film.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Try as hard as he might, Chris Pine can't rise above this predictable story.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: The Contractor's main objective is to build a solid foundation with a strong cast and a good script and pay it off with well-choreographed action sequences ...
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: The plot has promise, if it were allowed to really get goofy and wild. Instead, this is an action snoozer where any quick distraction might make you forget to watch the rest.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: 'The Contractor" builds solid action.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Pine still has the charm and sensibility to be Hollywood's Best Chris. But first he needs to find Hollywood's Best Role for Chris Pine.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: There is a bleak poetry to Davis script, as the men reckon with the things theyve done as lifelong warriors. Theres no pontificating, just a few choice words and details that add nuance to a story, or flip it on its back.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Putting Pine and Foster together again writes a check that the film ultimately isnt interested in cashing.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: The plot is faintly ludicrous, the emotional beats dont really land, and the whole thing feels both bloated and rushed, despite clocking it at just 103 minutes.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: In a crowded field of lone-man operators-against-the-world action films, The Contractor doesn’t do anything well enough to finish the job.
reviews.author: Adam Mullins-Khatib

reviews.text: THE CONTRACTOR seems to be two movies at war with each other, with the end result that neither one really works.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: Saleh crafts an agreeable-enough man-on-the-run thriller - a sturdy, workmanlike offering that occasionally rises above its cliched action movie husk.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: If soul-shattering mercenary work is the best option America's returning military operators have, as this film suggests, then America is not taking care of it's own. Definitely worth watching.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: While his character is intended to be lost and powerless, Pine seems adrift in another way, too – a star without a proper star vehicle.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: There’s enough here to make The Contractor watchable even as we close the door on it ever being good.
reviews.author: Matthew Monagle

reviews.text: Riddled with too many plot holes to make an impact.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Pine does a great deal of heavy lifting to carry the burden of giving a resonant and emotive performance that fills in the gaps in the script.
reviews.author: Ferdosa Abdi

reviews.text: This hollow assembly-line thriller pushes aside any meaningful exploration of Harpers moral conflict between loyalty and bitterness in favor of cliched set pieces.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: There’s something comfortingly unflashy about The Contractor: the action isn’t earth-shatteringly exciting, but it’s clearly shot, with enough jolts of vitality to keep the plot spinning.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Pine, as he has ably demonstrated elsewhere, is a solid action hero. Foster gives a rich, complex performance.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: Utterly cliched and predictable, The Contractor is at least never less than watchable thanks to the efforts of the vastly overqualified Chris Pine and Ben Foster.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: The Contractor isn't a great film, but I enjoyed watching Pine move out of his comfort zone once again and try something new.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: A fair, well-acted movie with all-too-relevant themes, this thriller is also stuck with a somber tone and middling pace that unfortunately bring little excitement or emotion to its familiar story.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Chris Pine and Ben Foster steady an uneven action thriller in their third collaboration. The Contractor tells an all too familiar story of betrayal and vengeance. But does it with tense gunplay that's ably delivered by the skilled leads.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: The film isn't gripping or engaging enough to overcome its lack of originality. It's not bad, it's just sort of blah.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Predictable and efficient, but disappointingly shallow, The Contractor is exactly the sort of film you expect it to be, without offering anything more.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: 'The Contractor' is fine, just fine, which is both the best and worst one can say about the film. This fact also makes it imminently forgettable.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: The core cast, Pine and Foster especially, are superb, while the screenplay gives them plenty to chew on. At a quickly moving 105 minutes, the film is worth the time investment.
reviews.author: Bobby LePire

reviews.text: An unsurprisingly strong reunion of Hell or High Water duo Chris Pine and Ben Foster, who reunite for another tale of masculinity and brotherhood
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The Contractor is a lesser pairing of Chris Pine and Ben Foster. There's good stuff here, though not quite enough to warrant a recommendation.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: The Contractor is a film that feels torn between those two aims, and only achieves middling fare that might not appeal to either audience.
reviews.author: Christian Valentin

reviews.text: [The Contractor] leaves you feeling drained and depressed. How’s that for a marquee blurb? Not a likely candidate, but not a misleading one either.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: It is all entertaining as far as it goes. So as a handsomely cast VOD entry, this gets a pass -- generic title and plot aside.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Pine and Foster sync up flawlessly, even when the dialogue fails them. This isn’t the reunion they deserve, but it’s nevertheless welcome.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Never lives up to its ambitions...employing important issues in a clumsily by-the-numbers and indifferently staged commercial thriller cheapens them rather than doing them justice.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: These weepy father issues (presented in short flashback) dont do much to give The Contractor much weight, which is a shame, because theres far more melancholy than there is dimly-lit action.
reviews.author: Fran Hoepfner

reviews.text: The filmmakers exploit the premise only insofar as it can take a paint-by-number action thriller with debts to The Bourne Identity and the Rambo movies.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: This is a movie that holds some early promise, but it's soon dismissed for a routine and simplifying plot.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Saleh is a bit clumsy with the rough stuff, but he still handles suspense reasonably well in this occasionally absorbing thriller.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: A fine Chris Pine performance can't balance The Contractor's otherwise bland and recyclable dad-movie nature.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: The Contractor is a thriller of divided ambitions, that earnestly wants to Say Something Important about the mistreatment of combat veterans by the very government that sends them to war, while also flirting with the opportunity for franchise potential.
reviews.author: Kevin Jagernauth

reviews.text: It's a standard-issue espionage story that makes an effort to engage with deeper themes about the treatment of veterans but falls short both as a suspense thriller and as a character drama.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: While The Contractor never quite reaches the heights it aspires to, the performances make it one of the better action thrillers of recent years.
reviews.author: John Townsend

reviews.text: A strong, character-driven action film with a terrific performance from Chris Pine.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: The Contractor showcases Chris Pine yet again as one of our most engaging actors, and though his reunion with Ben Foster deserved something heartier, it remains an entertaining enough watch.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: Movies can lose points for lack of originality only to regain them in execution. The Contractor, however, fails in both regards.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: A more thoughtful action drama than the norm aided by the Pine-Foster reunion and well-executed realistic fight scenes.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: The Contractor chooses to take a fascinating subject and plug it into the most generic thriller plot imaginable.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Offers enough of the familiar to entice fans of the genre while bringing the nuance needed to attract those who may normally ignore it. Great chemistry between Chris Pine and Ben Foster.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Muir

reviews.text: Surpasses expectations by proving itself to be a worthy entry into a specific genre.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Unfortunately, the writer feels that a tense drama must have more gun fighting scenes than the Netflix film Extraction.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: THE CONTRACTOR should have been a much better movie. As it is, its a mediocre effort --- and a waste of a lot of talent.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Pine is as sympathetic a protagonist as anyone these days, but Davis script is not quite as thrilling as it might have been.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: The Contractor is a strong action-drama with serious issues at its center. It does go from a message film into straight action once things get really going, but it does have its heart in the right place.
reviews.author: Emilie Black

reviews.text: What makes his and Saleh's work better than those contrivances is that they are trying to say something with those familiar machinations. While not an anti-military film, it is an anti-propaganda one.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Saleh's film lacks the claustrophobic atmosphere needed to transform a military adventure into a bona fide political thriller.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: The narrative does start on critical subjects that need to be discussed among military veterans, but that doesnt excuse it from descending into cliché stupidity
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: A solid, engaging action thriller, that once again showcases the great chemistry between actors Chris Pine and Ben Foster. Full review in Spanish
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The Contractor may not have the greatest action scenes or ending, but its heart – which it wears on its sleeve -- still makes it worth watching. Chris Pine gives a superb performance.
reviews.author: Adam Bankhurst

reviews.text: Saleh’s latest is a head above something like the dead-eyed Chris Hemsworth title Extraction, but it squanders the talents of an intriguing cast in what eventually feels like a conventional action thriller.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: A taut, smart thriller that plays against expectations, Tarik Saleh's The Contractor is an intriguing actioner that elevates itself above other genre entries with its insightful look at the plight of displaced soldiers.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Is there anything particularly novel about The Contractor? Nope, but thats fine.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: Far beyond the seen-it-all-before action and the predictable sprint towards the surprising twist ending that is neither a twist nor a surprise, the biggest disappointment of this film is the unfulfilled promise of Pine and Foster back together again.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: Not much to find here in the way of thrills or pathos.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: The films rote action-movie plotting is calibrated in a ponderously straight-faced way so as to give it some semblance of gravity.
reviews.author: Mark Hanson

reviews.text: The Contractor is a middling action thriller with some strong performances.
reviews.author: Danielle Ryan

reviews.text: The Contractor zeroes in on the soldiers who are trained to kill and often taken for granted. But it never stoops to empty flag-waving rhetoric. Instead, it asks what the protectors are protecting us from.
reviews.author: Sheri Linden

reviews.text: Being a solid cut above average is good enough, given so much formulaic mediocrity among thrillers cluttering the streaming market.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

synopsis: Chris Pine stars in the action-packed thriller as Special Forces Sergeant James Harper, who is involuntarily discharged from the Army and cut-off from his pension. In debt, out of options and desperate to provide for his family, Harper contracts with a private underground military force. When the very first assignment goes awry, the elite soldier finds himself hunted and on the run, caught in a dangerous conspiracy and fighting to stay alive long enough to get home and uncover the true motives of those who betrayed him.
